requirement:
`habeas author <full-name> [--config <name>] [--missing | --force] [--stdout] [-v|--verbose]`
MUST author the evidence of one existing requirement or named example in the
current project, under {cite}`requirements.authoring.refresh`. It MUST report the
selected subject, backend, model, evidence destination, and usage-record path on
completion. The evidence destination MUST identify the evidence-file path by
default or stdout when `--stdout` is selected. In stdout mode, the completion
report and diagnostics MUST go to stderr. `author-evidence` MUST remain an alias
for the single-subject command.
rationale:
The reviewed tests cover every obligation in `requirements.authoring.invocation`. Obligations that belong to the cited `requirements.authoring.refresh` are checked as applied to this command. I did not request any implementation source.

**Authoring one existing subject (requirement or example)**
- `fn[ollama_cli_delivers_sources_records_fixme_and_keeps_usage_content_free]` runs `author-evidence SUBJECT` and asserts the written evidence record: determination, rationale, `requirement` text and inputs.
- `fn[initial_prompt_substitutes_subject_and_mandatory_inputs_into_the_template]` runs `author` for both a requirement and a named example. For each it checks the `Evidence:` path and that the record has the `requirement` or `example` field for that kind.
- `fn[author_rejects_unknown_subjects_and_conflicting_targets]` shows that an unknown name such as `requirements.absent` fails and names the subject in stderr. It also shows that the subject given together with `--all` exits with code 2 and "cannot be used with", leaving existing evidence untouched.
- `fn[an_explicit_configuration_selects_the_nondefault_workspace_profile]` and `fn[authoring_uses_nearest_workspace_configuration_without_a_user_file]` run from a nested directory of the current project.

**Option syntax**
- `--config <name>`: `fn[an_explicit_configuration_selects_the_nondefault_workspace_profile]` selects the non-default profile. It asserts the request model and key, and the usage record's `model` and `backend`.
- `--missing` and `--force`: `fn[missing_keeps_current_records_and_force_reassesses_every_selected_subject]` covers the default and explicit `--missing` (nothing is assessed, no model is called). It covers `--force` reassessing, mutual exclusion, and `--stdout` implying `--force`. It also covers `--stdout --missing` being rejected and the "skipped as current" report. It runs the `author-evidence` alias with a broken configuration, which shows that no configuration is resolved when nothing needs assessment.
- `--stdout`: `fn[stdout_emits_only_evidence_json_without_changing_project_files]`.
- `-v` and `--verbose`: `fn[verbose_single_author_reports_only_false_rationale_without_source_inputs]` and the verbose cases in the stdout test.

**Completion report contents**
- By default, `fn[ollama_cli_delivers_sources_records_fixme_and_keeps_usage_content_free]` asserts that stdout starts with `SUBJECT: ollama / MODEL`. That line names the subject, backend and model. The test also asserts an `Evidence:` line whose path ends in `evidence/SUBJECT.json` and canonicalizes to the project's evidence file, and a `Usage:` line.
- `fn[initial_prompt_substitutes_subject_and_mandatory_inputs_into_the_template]` repeats the subject and backend line and the evidence path. It also asserts that the usage path is an existing file.

**Stdout mode**
- `fn[stdout_emits_only_evidence_json_without_changing_project_files]` parses all of stdout as a single JSON evidence record, so no report or diagnostic text can be on stdout.
- The same test asserts that stderr contains the `SUBJECT: ollama / MODEL` line, `Evidence: stdout\n` and the `Usage:` path of an existing file. It also asserts that no evidence file is written or changed, including when the `evidence` directory is absent.
- `fn[missing_duplicate_and_invalid_submissions_preserve_existing_evidence]` covers failures with `--stdout`: stdout is empty and the evidence file is unchanged.

**Alias**
- `author-evidence` is the command used in the report tests, the stdout tests and the failure tests. It is also used in the `--missing` batch scenario and in the rejection of the alias given with `--all`. This confirms it behaves as the single-subject command.

No relevant obligation is untested or unasserted, and there are no acknowledged gaps.

text: :::{req} invocation
`habeas author <full-name> [--config <name>] [--missing | --force] [--stdout] [-v|--verbose]`
MUST author the evidence of one existing requirement or named example in the
current project, under {cite}`requirements.authoring.refresh`. It MUST report the
selected subject, backend, model, evidence destination, and usage-record path on
completion. The evidence destination MUST identify the evidence-file path by
default or stdout when `--stdout` is selected. In stdout mode, the completion
report and diagnostics MUST go to stderr. `author-evidence` MUST remain an alias
for the single-subject command.
:::{req} refresh
Every `habeas author` form MUST accept `--missing` and `--force`, which are
mutually exclusive; `--missing` MUST be the default. Under `--missing`, the
command MUST assess only the selected subjects whose evidence is missing, stale,
or invalid, and MUST preserve every current record without invoking a model,
including accepted FIXME judgments and current false judgments; a current false
judgment is reassessed only when its subject or inputs change or `--force` is
given. Under `--force`, the command MUST assess every selected subject. `--stdout`
MUST imply `--force`, because it writes no evidence. The command MUST report the
number of selected subjects it skipped as current. When no assessment is needed,
the command MUST succeed without resolving model configuration or credentials.
